2.
Since these two bail applications arise out of one and same case record, the same are heard together and disposed of by this common order with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties.

3. These are second bail applications U/S.439 of CrPC by the Petitioners for grant of bail in connection with Satyabadi PS Case No.225 of 2022 corresponding to Spl. G.R. Case No.78 of 2022 pending in the file of learned Adhoc A.S.J(FTSC), Puri, for commission of offences punishable U/S.
376(DA) of IPC r/w. Section 6 of the POCSO Act, on the allegation of committing gang rape and penetrative sexual assault upon the victim aged about 14 years.

4. At the outset, it is stated by the respective counsels for the petitioners that these are the 2nd bail applications of the Petitioners-Muna @ Susanta Kumar Nayak in BLAPL No.8927 of 2024 and Dipti Ranjan Swain in BLAPL No.9733 of 2024, but no bail application of each of Petitioners is pending Unknown vs State Of Orissa And Another ...

1 before any other forum except these two bail applications.

5. Heard, Mr. Tara Prasad Mohapatra, learned counsel for the Petitioner-Muna @ Susanta Kumar Nayak in BLAPL No.8927 of 2024, Mr. Bikram Chandra Ghadei, learned counsel for the Petitioner- Dipti Ranjan Swain in BLAPL No.9733 of 2024, Mr. Mohendra Kumar Mohapatro, learned counsel for the victim and Mr. B.P. Nayak, learned AGA in the matter and perused the record.

Mr.
Mohapatro, learned counsel for the victim and Mr. B.P. Nayak, learned AGA in tandem opposes the bail application of the Petitioners by stating inter-alia that 13 out of 16 charge-sheeted witnesses have already been examined and, therefore, release of the Petitioners at this stage would impede the trial.
6.

It is not disputed that both the Petitioners are in custody since 08.08.2022, but in the meanwhile,
around more than two years have elapsed, however, the trial has not yet been concluded.
In the aforesaid backdrop, when the evidence of the victim is taken into consideration, it appears that the victim has not alleged against the Petitioners for sexually exploiting her.

7. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstance and taking into account the rival submissions and regard being had to the pre-trial detention of the Petitioners in custody and keeping in view the trial having not concluded despite the mandate of Sec. 35(2) of the POCSO Act, this Court without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, admits each of the Petitioners to bail.
8. Hence, these two bail applications of the Petitioners Muna @ Susanta Kumar Nayak in BLAPL No.8927 of 2024 and Dipti Ranjan Swain in BLAPL No.9733 of 2024 stand allowed.

Accordingly,
the Petitioners-Muna @ Susanta Kumar Nayak & Dipti Ranjan Swain are allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) only each with two solvent sureties for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the petitioners shall not commit any offence while on bail,
(ii) the petitioners in the course of trial shall attend the trial Court on each date of posting without fail unless their attendance is dispensed with.

In case the Petitioners fail without sufficient cause to appear in the Court in accordance with the terms of the bail, the learned trial Court may proceed against the Petitioners for offence U/S.229-A of IPC in accordance with law,
(iii) the petitioners shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till disposal of the case by giving their present address of stay.

It is clarified that the Court in seisin of the case will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioners without further reference to this Court, if any of the above conditions are violated or a case for cancellation of bail is otherwise made out.

In the wake of aforesaid, the subsequent involvement of the petitioners in future for any grave/similar offence on prima facie accusations may be treated as a ground for cancellation of bail in this case.
